modulesTouched.path: scripts/docs/inventories/ (remaining 14 family extractors: adrs, areas, chores, ci-gates, classes, config, context-map, pages, redis-keys, schemas, skills, streams, tier-paths, units-scripts)

invariants: Verifier Core is untouched: no edit to .github/workflows/ci.yml, src/untouchable.ts, src/tier-classifier.ts or scripts/tier-classify.ts. MUTATION_GATE_BLOCKING stays unset and every killFloor in src/mutation-gate-inputs.ts keeps its value — this slice makes the advisory number honest, it does not change what blocks a merge.

The read ratchet runs inside the required `test` job as a top-level node:test describe (never an advisory workflow or ast-grep rule). It reads only test/*.test.mts and its own fixture — no git history, no GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, no Redis, no network — and the failure message prints the exact fixture line to add plus the rule id STD-TEST-RUN-THE-CODE.

Detection is per FILE and gates only CODE paths: a test file is a code reader iff it (a) calls a filesystem read (readFileSync/readFile/readdirSync/readdir) and (b) contains a string literal that resolves under src/, scripts/, bin/ or dashboard/src/, or ends in .sh/.py/.mjs. Reads of docs/, config/, .github/, CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, playbooks, *.md and test/fixtures are never gated; `import` statements never count as reads; comments are stripped before scanning.

The fixture test/fixtures/test-source-read-baseline.json maps each allowed test file to exactly one kind from the closed set {drift-guard, invariant-lint, dashboard-pin, behaviour, grandfathered}. Unknown kind → fail. A row whose file no longer exists or no longer reads a code path → fail (stale row, delete it). An unlisted code-reading file → fail. The fixture changes only by a deliberate, reviewable one-line diff.

Day one is green: the fixture is seeded from the live tree, kinds assigned from the #5188 per-file classification (research doc 2026-10-24); anything structure-sensitive, mixed or uncertain is `grandfathered`. The ratchet test lists ITSELF as `invariant-lint` (its regex literals would otherwise self-match). Grandfathered rows only shrink: the test cannot see history, so this is the reviewer's rule under STD-TEST-RUN-THE-CODE and is stated in the test header; the test does enforce that a grandfathered row names an existing file.

CODING_STANDARDS.md § Tests STD-TEST-RUN-THE-CODE gets `enforced-by: reviewer, test/test-source-read-ratchet.test.mts` (the standards-loader validates the path exists) and test/fixtures/coding-standards-baseline.json is regenerated for the word delta; no other rule text changes (S5 #5261 owns the packet inlining).

Mutant validity is decided at GENERATION time in src/mutation.ts: for each candidate line, the mutated file is checked with typescript.transpileModule({ reportDiagnostics: true, fileName: <mutant path> }) and is unparseable iff its syntactic diagnostic count exceeds the unmutated file's baseline count (computed once per file). An unparseable mutant is never written to disk and never runs tests; it is recorded as { skipped: true, error: 'unparseable mutant (<mutator>): <first diagnostic>' }, counted in totalMutants and skipped, and excluded from the kill-rate denominator by the existing conclusiveMutants(). It consumes neither a maxMutants slot nor time budget.

swap-comparison keeps looking: ===/!== first as today; then every `>` occurrence left-to-right, then every `<`, taking the first candidate that parses; only when none parses does the line yield the single skipped unparseable result. The four mutators stay four — no literal mutator — and the shape of MutationTestReport is unchanged except for one additive counter (skippedUnparseable) that scripts/ci/mutation-check.ts also prints in its summary JSON.

`typescript` is loaded lazily (dynamic import inside runMutationTests), never at module top level: src/mutation.ts is transitively imported by the running service (src/retro-inputs.ts → src/mutation-gate-inputs.ts → src/mutation.ts). typescript stays a devDependency; the ADR-0005 runtime allowlist is unchanged. scripts/target/mutation-check.ts inherits the fix unchanged because it shares the runner; passing fileName lets .tsx parse under the right grammar.

Every generated inventory row's `source` becomes { path } — no `line` anywhere under docs/generated/ — and the envelope schemaVersion moves 1 → 2 in every family (counts included). Extractors may still use line numbers internally (env-vars read-site dedup/ordering, tier-paths fail messages) but nothing reaches the emitted rows; row ORDER is unchanged so the regeneration diff is deletions only, and `npm run docs:inventories` followed by the drift guard is green and byte-deterministic.

The dashboard /docs catalogues render `source.path` and link via sourceUrl(path) (already tolerant of a missing line); no React key and no test depends on `source.line` afterwards. ADR-0034 §10 gets a one-line amendment: inventories record the source file path, never a line number (#5262).

Order of work follows the CLAUDE.md remove-behaviour rule: first rewrite the existing line pins (test/generated-inventories-drift.test.mts routes fixture ~L552-554 and the buildChoreRows string ~L631, test/docs-classes-skills.test.mts ~L134, test/docs-adrs.test.mts fixture ~L95) to assert path-only, watch them go red, then change the generator, then regenerate. The new test file is baselined in the same PR: node scripts/test/suite-count-check.mjs --update-baseline --only test/test-source-read-ratchet.test.mts (and the test-subject sprawl baseline if it objects to the new scan module's single test file).

The PR body's `## Files in scope` enumerates every touched path above (the issue's list is incomplete and names a non-existent scripts/docs/inventories.ts); scope-check reads the PR body live. Expected tier stays T3 (dashboard JSX edits are T2, src/scripts are T3; the PR classifies to the deepest). No ratchet/extractor code throws on malformed input — they return result objects and the test asserts on them.

npm test, npm run typecheck:test and tsc pass; the mutation change is itself exercised by new cases in test/mutation.test.mts: (1) a `new Map<string, X>()` line yields no running mutant and one skipped unparseable result; (2) a line holding both a generic and a real comparison yields a parseable swap on the comparison; (3) a report with only unparseable mutants reaches the existing all-skipped no-signal branch of scripts/ci/mutation-check.ts.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Enforce the read rule as an advisory ast-grep rule or a sibling workflow instead of a required test
rejectedAlternatives.why: Advisory workflows always exit 0 and no seam check in this repo is a required check (operator memory); only checks inside the required `test` job block. #5189 decided the `test` job explicitly; test-file-sprawl-guard and api-500-catch-ratchet are the precedent.
Needs an AST walk of test bodies to attribute a read to a case; #5189 chose per-file as coarse but cheap, and the ~4 conversion issues shrink rows file by file anyway.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: An --update-baseline regenerator that adds new rows automatically
rejectedAlternatives.why: Would turn the fixture into a rubber stamp. A new row must name a sanctioned kind that the reviewer judges in a one-line diff. Only a read-only --print helper that lists unlisted readers is provided.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Make the test itself prove that grandfathered rows only shrink (git history / previous fixture)
rejectedAlternatives.why: Re-introduces exactly the out-of-tree coupling #4132 removed (GITHUB_EVENT_PATH / git state inside the suite) with reds that cannot self-clear. Shrink-only is a reviewer rule; the test enforces existence and kind.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Keep #5189's four kinds (drift-guard, invariant-lint, dashboard-pin, grandfathered) with no `behaviour` kind
rejectedAlternatives.why: #5188 found 47 files whose code reads are legitimate INPUT to code they run (copy a script into a sandbox, feed a file to a parser). Forcing them into `grandfathered` tells them to shrink, contradicting STD-TEST-RUN-THE-CODE's own first sentence. `behaviour` is the rule's sanctioned 'input to code it runs' clause made explicit.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Fix swap-comparison with regex heuristics that skip type positions (e.g. `<` after an identifier, `>(` closers)
rejectedAlternatives.why: Brittle across generics, arrow returns and casts; transpileModule is ground truth for 'does it parse', and the research measured it on all 7,786 candidates. It also covers the (currently zero) parse breaks of the other three mutators for free.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Check parseability at run time, after writeFile, and mark skipped then
rejectedAlternatives.why: The dead mutant would already have taken a maxMutants slot and a time-budget tick; 12 of 26 non-skipped CI runs end in budget exhaustion, so the ~28% should never enter the candidate list.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Static top-level `import ts from 'typescript'` in src/mutation.ts
rejectedAlternatives.why: src/mutation.ts is reachable from the running service (retro-inputs → mutation-gate-inputs → mutation), so the compiler would load into the orchestrator process for a CI-only path. Dynamic import keeps it CI-only.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Inject an isParseable function through runMutationTests opts from the two CI scripts
rejectedAlternatives.why: Two call sites to keep in lockstep and a default-off path that leaves the Target gate inflated; the runner owns the check so both gates are honest by construction.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Turn on MUTATION_GATE_BLOCKING or retune the 55% T3 floor in this slice
rejectedAlternatives.why: ci.yml is Verifier Core (T4) and ADR-0046 defers the blocking decision until ~30 src/ PRs of honest rates exist; the floor was tuned on inflated rates and must be re-measured, not guessed.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Keep `line` in the inventories but exclude it from the drift comparison
rejectedAlternatives.why: The cost is git churn of a COMMITTED artifact (32 of the last 200 master commits regenerated for line shifts alone), not the comparison; the field has to leave the file.
A silent format change for any consumer that read source.line; the bump is one literal per family and the envelope type already pins it.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Three PRs (ratchet, mutation validity, line drop)
rejectedAlternatives.why: All three are T3, independent and small; the system is quota-bound (throughput audit), so three CI/QA rounds cost more than one PR with three clean commits. The regen diff is deletions only.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Add `ratchet`, `drift guard`, `grandfathered` to CONTEXT.md as glossary gaps
rejectedAlternatives.why: General engineering vocabulary already used uniformly across test headers, CLAUDE.md and ADR-0046, not Hydra domain concepts; CONTEXT.md is glossary-only for domain language.

qaTrace.q: Premise check: is #5262 still open work on origin/master (250665e15), or already shipped / duplicated?
qaTrace.a: Open work. No test/test-source-read-ratchet.test.mts, no test/fixtures/test-source-read-baseline.json; src/mutation.ts still has the single-shot swap-comparison and no parse check; docs/generated/ still carries 1,421 `"line":` fields (env-vars 830, routes 134, schemas 94, redis-keys 87, ...). Blocker #5260 (S4) is CLOSED and merged (2c5abd9ee), so the dependency is satisfied. No open PR references #5262. No existing design concept and no research report for issue-5262.

qaTrace.q: Does the issue's file list match the code? Which files does the acceptance criteria actually require?
qaTrace.a: No. `scripts/docs/inventories.ts` does not exist — the generator is scripts/docs/generate-inventories.ts plus 16 family extractors under scripts/docs/inventories/ with the row types in envelope.ts. The mutation AC needs src/mutation.ts (runner) and scripts/ci/mutation-check.ts (summary) which the issue omits. Line-field pins live in test/generated-inventories-drift.test.mts, test/docs-classes-skills.test.mts, test/docs-adrs.test.mts and two dashboard JSX catalogue pages. CODING_STANDARDS.md must point STD-TEST-RUN-THE-CODE's enforced-by at the new test (#5189 table). The design concept's modulesTouched is the corrected list; the PR body must enumerate it because scope-check reads the body.

qaTrace.q: Where does the read-ratchet logic live: inside the test file or an importable module?
qaTrace.a: An importable pure module scripts/ci/test-source-read-scan.ts (mirrors scripts/ci/test-subject-map.ts behind test-file-sprawl-guard) exporting the detector and the fixture comparison; the test imports it, runs it over the live tree, and pins the detection rules against synthetic sources in trailing fixture cases (the generated-inventories-drift pattern). A .test.mts cannot be imported for rule tests, so self-contained would mean untested rules.

qaTrace.q: What exactly counts as a 'read of a code path' — how coarse, what is excluded, how is self-matching avoided?
qaTrace.a: Per file: fs read call present AND a string literal resolving under src/, scripts/, bin/, dashboard/src/, or ending .sh/.py/.mjs, after stripping comments. Imports are not reads. docs/, config/, .github/, *.md, test/fixtures are never gated — #5189: 'does not gate docs, playbook or config reads'. The ratchet test itself contains those prefixes as regex literals, so it is listed in the fixture as invariant-lint rather than special-cased in code. A rough live grep gives ~180 matching files; the seed is whatever the scanner reports, kinds from #5188.

qaTrace.q: What kinds does the fixture allow, and how are the ~47 legitimate behaviour readers classified?
qaTrace.a: {drift-guard, invariant-lint, dashboard-pin, behaviour, grandfathered}. #5189 listed four; `behaviour` is added because STD-TEST-RUN-THE-CODE itself sanctions reading repo text as input to code the test runs, and 47 of #5188's files are exactly that — labelling them grandfathered would order them to shrink. Uncertain or mixed files default to grandfathered (shrink-only is the safe default; promotion is a reviewed one-line diff later).

qaTrace.q: Can the test enforce 'grandfathered rows only shrink'?
qaTrace.a: Not without history, and reading git/GITHUB_EVENT_PATH from the suite is the coupling #4132 removed. The test enforces what it can see — every row's file exists, still reads code, and names a known kind; no unlisted reader — and the shrink-only rule is the reviewer's under STD-TEST-RUN-THE-CODE, stated in the test header. A new grandfathered row is a visible diff the Standards reviewer rejects.

qaTrace.q: Mutation gate: where is the parse check applied, with what oracle, and what is the baseline?
qaTrace.a: At generation time in generateMutations/runMutationTests, with typescript.transpileModule({reportDiagnostics:true, fileName}) — verified locally on typescript 6.0.2: a valid generic line yields 0 syntactic diagnostics, the generic-swap mutant 2, a real `>`→`<` swap 0. Baseline = the unmutated file's diagnostic count (computed once per file) so files with pre-existing diagnostics are not all-skipped. Unparseable → recorded skipped with an error reason, no write, no test run, no cap slot, no budget. conclusiveMutants() already excludes skipped, so killRate is honest without touching the formula; the summary gains an additive skippedUnparseable counter.

qaTrace.q: Does swap-comparison need to change beyond the check?
qaTrace.a: Yes, per #5189: it must look past an invalid swap to a real comparison on the same line, otherwise a line like `const m = new Map<string, X>(); if (a > b)` loses its only real mutant. Candidate order: ===, !==, each `>` left-to-right, each `<`; first parseable wins; none → one skipped result. Still one mutant per line, still four mutators, still no literal mutator (tautology measured rare).

qaTrace.q: Is importing `typescript` from src/ acceptable under ADR-0005 and the service runtime?
qaTrace.a: As a lazy dynamic import, yes. typescript is a devDependency used only on CI paths; .dependency-cruiser.cjs has no dev-dep rule and the ADR-0005 allowlist concerns service runtime deps. But src/mutation.ts IS reachable from the service (retro-inputs → mutation-gate-inputs → mutation), so a top-level import would load the compiler into the orchestrator process — hence `await import('typescript')` inside runMutationTests only. The Target gate shares the runner and inherits the fix.

qaTrace.q: What is the new inventory format contract and who consumes `line` today?
qaTrace.a: SourceRef and RouteRow.source become { path }; schemaVersion 1 → 2 in envelope.ts, every family and counts. Consumers: dashboard Catalogue.jsx / RoutesCatalogue.jsx (render path:line, call sourceUrl(path, line) which already tolerates undefined, and use line in React keys), parity.ts (path only, unaffected), and three tests that pin line values. Extractors keep line internally where it orders or dedups (env-vars read sites) — only the emitted row drops it, so row order and therefore the regen diff stay deletion-only.

qaTrace.q: Which docs/ADR text needs amending for the line drop?
qaTrace.a: ADR-0024's catalogue paragraph already lists method/path/stability/consumers without line, so no change there. ADR-0034 §10 never mentions line numbers; add a one-line amendment stating inventories record source path, never line (#5262), so the decision is findable. The envelope.ts doc comments ('file + line of the router.<verb>( token', '1-based line') are rewritten.

qaTrace.q: One PR or three, and what tier?
qaTrace.a: One PR, three commits (ratchet + standards pointer; mutant validity; line drop + regen + ADR note). All T3 by path (scripts/, src/, docs/generated/; the two JSX edits are T2); no Verifier Core path. The new test file requires the suite-count baseline regeneration in the same PR (BLOCKING file-set verdict otherwise), and possibly the test-subject sprawl baseline for the new scan module.

qaTrace.q: Glossary: do 'ratchet', 'drift guard', 'kind-tagged fixture', 'grandfathered' need CONTEXT.md entries?
qaTrace.a: No — general engineering vocabulary used uniformly across the repo (adr-roster, skill-size-ratchet, api-500-catch-ratchet headers; CLAUDE.md; ADR-0046 Decision 4), not Hydra domain concepts. Grounded terms used by this design: Pre-merge Gate (the ratchet joins its required `test` job; mutation-test stays a member that cannot fail on rate), Verifier Core (untouched), Modification Tier (T3), Design Concept (this artifact). glossaryGaps is empty.

qaTrace.q: Does any question need a prototype sub-dispatch?
qaTrace.a: No. The only logic question — can transpileModule discriminate parseable from unparseable single-line mutants with a per-file baseline — was already measured in the #5188 research over all 7,786 candidates and re-verified here with a three-line check on typescript 6.0.2 (0 / 2 / 0 diagnostics). No sandbox was created, so nothing to clean up.
